verdict.rationale: A GPU is programmatically driven through vendor APIs, and NVIDIA's first-party CUDA Toolkit documents a runtime library, compiler, and C++/Python tile-kernel programming models for its GPUs. An independent Phoronix test ran 60+ CUDA/OptiX/OpenCL/Vulkan benchmarks on the 5090, confirming the card is driven through these APIs. The 404 OpenAPI probes concern a web REST spec, which does not apply to hardware. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that the CUDA APIs support the RTX 5090, and evidence of API reference depth (function-level docs) or agent-oriented usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The toolkit includes GPU-accelerated libraries, debugging and optimization tools, a C/C++ compiler, and a runtime library.
It is built on top of the CUDA Tile IR specification and allows you to write tile kernels in Python.
across 60+ CUDA/OptiX/OpenCL/Vulkan benchmarks the 5090 delivered 1.42x the RTX 4090's performance
